title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
description: For every elliptic curve E over the rational numbers, determine whether the rank of the finitely generated group E(Q) equals the order of vanishing of its L-function L(E,s) at s=1. Thus, if r is the number of independent rational points of infinite order, the first nonzero term in the Taylor expansion at s=1 should have degree r. The target is this equality in full generality over Q. The refined conjecture about the leading coefficient is a related stronger statement, rather than an additional requirement in Wiles's displayed Millennium problem.

title: Hodge conjecture
description: For every smooth projective algebraic variety X over the complex numbers and every integer p, determine whether each rational cohomology class in H^(2p)(X,Q) that has Hodge type (p,p) is a rational linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic cycles of codimension p. The question connects topological information in cohomology with subvarieties defined by algebraic equations. The target is the general rational Hodge conjecture for this class of varieties, with rational coefficients in the combination; an integral-coefficient variant or a statement about arbitrary complex manifolds is a different assertion.

title: Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness
description: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with positive viscosity, establish one of Fefferman's four alternatives. (A) Every smooth divergence-free initial velocity on R^3, rapidly decaying with all derivatives, admits a global smooth velocity-pressure solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy when the external force is zero. (B) Every smooth divergence-free spatially periodic initial velocity admits a global smooth solution with spatially periodic velocity when the force is zero. (C) Some such rapidly decaying initial velocity and some smooth force on R^3 admit no global smooth solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy; the force and all its derivatives must decay faster than every inverse power of 1+|x|+t. (D) Some smooth periodic divergence-free initial velocity and smooth periodic force admit no global smooth solution with periodic velocity; the force and all its derivatives must decay faster than every inverse power of 1+t. The periodic domain is R^3/Z^3. Any one alternative meets the stated mathematical target.

title: P versus NP
description: Determine whether P equals NP in the standard deterministic and nondeterministic Turing-machine model. P contains decision problems solvable in polynomial time; NP contains decision problems whose affirmative answers have certificates of polynomial length that a deterministic algorithm can check in polynomial time. A resolution must establish whether every problem in NP has a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, or whether at least one does not. The target concerns worst-case asymptotic computational complexity for unrestricted algorithms, rather than success on a finite collection of instances or an improvement to one particular algorithm.

title: Riemann hypothesis
description: Determine whether every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2. The function is initially defined by the series sum of n^(-s) for real part of s greater than 1, and extends meromorphically to the complex plane with a pole at s=1. Its negative even integer zeros are the trivial zeros; the conjecture concerns all the remaining zeros. The target is a proof covering every nontrivial zero or a rigorous counterexample. Verifying any finite range of zeros alone does not settle this universal statement.

title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
description: For every compact simple gauge group G, rigorously construct a nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 and establish a positive, finite mass gap. Existence must satisfy axiomatic requirements at least as strong as the Wightman or Osterwalder-Schrader formulations cited in the official statement, with appropriate gauge-invariant local fields and short-distance behavior. With vacuum energy normalized to zero, a mass gap means the Hamiltonian has no spectrum in (0,Delta) for some Delta>0, with the supremum of admissible gaps finite. The target requires the four-dimensional continuum theory, not only a lattice approximation or the classical equations.
